sd.step1: Prepare, once per project. With Arduino connected by USB cable, “Prepare Arduino” sends it the sensors, pins and rates, saves them (they stay even when it’s off) and tests the card.
sd.step2: Record. Unplug the cable and power Arduino from a power bank or a 9 V battery. {detail}
sd.step2Button: Press the button to start and press it again to stop: each recording is a new file.
sd.step2Free: It records from when you switch it on until you switch it off (add a button to decide when yourself). Data is saved every 2 seconds: cutting the power loses at most the last few moments.
sd.step3: Import. Put the card in the computer (or in the phone with an adapter) and choose the files LOG00001.CSV, LOG00002.CSV…: they become Notebook measurements, with the usual quantities and charts.
sd.liveNote: If you connect the app while Arduino is recording, the recording is closed and you measure as usual.
sd.prepareTitle: Send and save the configuration, then test the card
sd.prepareNeedsUsb: Connect Arduino with the USB cable first
sd.prepareHint: “Prepare Arduino” is enabled when Arduino is connected by USB cable (firmware v1.5).

modules.ntcNoPolarity: The thermistor and the resistor have no polarity.
modules.ldrNoPolarity: The photoresistor and the resistor have no polarity.
modules.ntcPosition: The thermistor is on the {side, select, gnd {GND side} other {5V side}}: this must match the “Position” option in the Components tab.
modules.ldrPosition: The photoresistor is on the {side, select, gnd {GND side} other {5V side}}: this must match the “Position” option in the Components tab.
modules.dhtNote: Check the pin order printed on your module: the diagram follows VCC, DATA, GND (4-pin sensor: VCC, DATA, free, GND; pick the package in the options). The 10 kΩ resistor between DATA and 5V is essential with the bare sensor; the 3-pin module already has it, but leaving it in does no harm.
modules.sonarNote: Point the sensor at a flat target, between 5 cm and 3 m away.
modules.gpsNoteRx: The RX wire (dashed) is optional, but the pin stays reserved. If you connect it, go through the 1 kΩ + 2 kΩ divider: the module’s RX only tolerates 3.3 V.
modules.gpsNoteAntenna: Antenna with the ceramic side facing the sky. The first fix outdoors takes from 30 s to a few minutes.
modules.analogNote: Never more than 5 V on the pin, and never mains electricity.
modules.ds18b20NoteWires: Probe wires: red VCC, yellow DATA, black GND.
modules.ds18b20NotePullup: Without the 4.7 kΩ resistor between DATA and 5V the probe doesn’t respond. If yours has the small board with screw terminals, it already has one.
modules.gateFast: On D2 and D3 the times are accurate to the microsecond.
modules.gateSlow: On D2 or D3 the times would be more accurate (to the microsecond).
modules.gateInverted: If the times come out inverted, change “When the beam is blocked” in the options.
modules.hx711NoteWires: Load cell on the HX711: red E+, black E−, white A−, green A+. If the weight goes the wrong way, swap white and green.
modules.hx711NoteCalibrate: To calibrate, weigh a known mass and adjust “counts per gram”.
modules.imuNoteOled: An OLED display can share the same SDA and SCL pins.
modules.imuNoteFix: Fix the module firmly to the object: if it moves, it measures its own vibrations.
modules.buttonNoteLegs: A 4-pin push button goes across the central gap: the two pins on the same side are always connected to each other.
modules.buttonNotePullup: No resistor: Arduino uses its internal pull-up resistor.
modules.buttonNoteUse: With the app connected it works like “Start” and “Stop”; with the SD card it starts and stops the recording.
modules.sdNoteModule: Use a module with a regulator and level shifter (almost all of them: “Micro SD Card Adapter”): it runs on 5V. Check the pin order printed on the module.
modules.sdNoteSpi: MISO, MOSI and SCK are always D12, D11 and D13: no other component can use them.
modules.sdNoteFat: Card formatted as FAT32 (up to 32 GB). Cards of 64 GB and up ship as exFAT: reformat them as FAT32.
modules.mlxNoteModule: Use the GY-906 module: it already has the regulator and the pull-up resistors, and tolerates 5 V. The bare sensor (small 4-pin metal can) runs on 3.3 V and can’t be wired like this.
modules.mlxNoteBus: It can share the same SDA and SCL pins as the display and the MPU-6050.
modules.mlxNoteCone: It sees a cone of about 90°: the farther away, the larger the area it measures. For a small surface stay 1–2 cm away.
modules.mlxNoteMetal: Shiny metal surfaces reflect the room’s infrared: cover them with matte tape or black paint and use ε = 0.95.
modules.oledNote: Check the order printed on the module: on some, VCC and GND are swapped.
modules.rgbNoteCommon: The longest pin is the common one.
modules.rgbNoteResistors: The 220 Ω resistors on each color protect the LED and Arduino’s pins. If your module already has them, leaving these in only makes the LED a little dimmer.
modules.buzzerNotePlus: The + is the longest pin (or “S” on the module).
modules.buzzerNoteResistor: The 100 Ω resistor limits the current: a bare passive buzzer draws more from the pin than it can supply.
modules.buzzerNoteKind: Connected to 5V, the active buzzer sounds; the passive one just clicks. Set the type in the options.
modules.btNoteDivider: The module’s RXD tolerates 3.3 V: the 1 kΩ and 2 kΩ resistors bring down the 5 V from D1.
modules.btNoteUpload: While you use the USB cable (uploading the firmware, “Prepare Arduino”, measuring over the cable) unplug the TXD → D0 wire: on the Uno the module would drown out the computer’s commands. For “Configure”, plug it in when the app asks.
modules.imuNoteAd0Low: XDA, XCL, AD0 and INT stay unconnected: with AD0 free the address is 0x68.
modules.imuNoteAd0High: AD0 goes to Arduino's 3.3V pin (not 5V: the chip runs at 3.3V), so this module answers at 0x69 and doesn't clash with the other MPU-6050.
modules.busJunction: shared: one wire from Arduino, then a branch for each module
modules.spsNoteCable: The SPS30 has a tiny JST ZHR-5 socket (1.5 mm pitch) that doesn't fit the breadboard: use a JST ZHR-5 to jumper-pin cable and plug its 5 pins into row e in order, pin 1 (VDD) first.
modules.spsNoteSel: SEL (pin 4) must reach GND before the sensor is powered, otherwise it starts in UART mode: wire everything with the USB cable unplugged. Never connect SEL to 5V (4 V maximum).
modules.spsNoteShort: Keep the I2C cable short (under 10 cm, as Sensirion recommends): long wires pick up interference.
modules.spsNoteAir: Leave the air inlet and outlet free and don't block the fan. It draws up to 80 mA: power Arduino from USB or a good power bank.
modules.spsNotePullups: The SPS30 has no pull-up resistors on SDA and SCL: here it's alone on the bus, so the two 10 kΩ resistors to 5V are needed.

board.aria: Realistic wiring diagram: Arduino, breadboard and sensors
board.powerPlace: Bring 5V and GND to the rails: the red rail (+) is 5V, the blue one (−) is GND.
board.placeResFirst: 10 kΩ resistor between {a} and {b}, {part} between {c} and {d}.
board.placePartFirst: {part} between {a} and {b}, 10 kΩ resistor between {c} and {d}.
board.leaveFree: {n, plural, one {Pin {list} stays free: no wire.} other {Pins {list} stay free: no wires.}}
board.busPlace: An Arduino header hole holds only one wire, but {n} modules use {pin}. One wire goes from {pin} into hole {a}; holes {a}–{e} of that column are connected, so each module plugs its {pin} wire into one of the other holes.
board.splitRails: On many full-size breadboards the red and blue lines along the rails break in the middle: there the two halves aren’t connected, so bridge each rail with a short jumper across the gap.
board.joinPlace: Put B{board} right of B{prev}, touching (they can snap together). Its rails aren’t connected to the others: join the top + rails with a red jumper and the top − rails with a black one.
board.bridgeNote: Carries power up to the top rails, where the modules plug in.
board.splitNote: Needed only if the red and blue lines break in the middle of the board.
board.joinNote: Each breadboard’s rails are separate: this joins them.
board.sideNote: Voltage divider, {side, select, gnd {GND side} other {5V side}}.
board.dividerNote: Voltage divider: turns Arduino’s 5V signal into 3.3V for {pin}.
board.pullupNote: Pull-up: holds {pin} at 5V when the line is idle.
board.seriesNote: In series with {pin}: limits the current.
board.busNote: Shared {pin} bus: holes a–e of this column are connected.
board.viaNote: {via, select, divider {Through a voltage divider (2 kΩ + 1 kΩ).} series {Through a {ohms} resistor.} pullup {With a {ohms} pull-up to 5V.} other {}}
